notes: Hand-verified against the scenario's own arithmetic before comparing to reference-model output. Lots: 100 units @ $10.00 (2026-01-01), 100 units @ $12.00 (2026-04-01), 100 units @ $15.00 (2027-01-01).

Sale 1 (2026-06-01, 150 units @ $20.00 = $3000.00 revenue): FIFO consumes the oldest lot first — 100 units @ $10.00 ($1000.00) fully empties lot 1, then 50 units @ $12.00 ($600.00) from lot 2. COGS = 1000.00 + 600.00 = 1600.00, not 150×$11.00 (an average cost) which would give the wrong 1650.00. Net income = 3000.00 − 1600.00 = 1400.00. Remaining inventory: 50 units @ $12.00 = $600.00.

Sale 2 (2027-06-01, 100 units @ $25.00 = $2500.00 revenue): FIFO consumes the remaining 50 units @ $12.00 ($600.00) from lot 2, then 50 units @ $15.00 ($750.00) from lot 3. COGS = 600.00 + 750.00 = 1350.00. Net income = 2500.00 − 1350.00 = 1150.00. Remaining inventory: 50 units @ $15.00 = $750.00.

2026-01 (January alone, just the first purchase — a purchase never touches the income statement, only the balance sheet): net income 0.00. Cash = 2200.00 (opening) − 1000.00 (purchase 1) = 1200.00. Inventory = 1000.00. Balance sheet: assets (1200.00 + 1000.00) 2200.00 = equity (owner_equity 2200.00 + current_period_earnings 0.00) 2200.00.

2026-06 (June alone — all of 2026's revenue activity happens in this one month; April's purchase already happened and nothing else occurs in 2026 before or after June): net income 1400.00 (as above). Cash: April left cash at 1200.00 − 1200.00 (purchase 2) = 0.00; June's sale brings in 3000.00 → 3000.00. This is also 2026's full-year ending cash, since nothing happens in 2026 after June. Inventory 600.00. Cash flow: net_income 1400.00 + inventory adjustment +1600.00 (inventory decreased by the COGS amount, a source of cash) = 3000.00, matching ending_cash 3000.00 − beginning_cash (end of May, still 0.00) = 3000.00.

2026-12 and 2026 (full year): December alone has zero activity (nothing happens between July and December), so December's own net income is 0.00, while the full year's net income (1400.00) equals June's alone, since June is 2026's only revenue-generating month. Balance sheet at year end (after the first closing): assets (cash 3000.00 + inventory 600.00) 3600.00 = equity (owner_equity 2200.00 + retained_earnings 1400.00) 3600.00.

2027-06 (June 2027 alone, after January's purchase 3): net income 1150.00 (as above). Cash: January left cash at 3000.00 − 1500.00 (purchase 3) = 1500.00; June's sale brings in 2500.00 → 4000.00. Inventory 750.00. Cash flow: net_income 1150.00 + inventory +1350.00 = 2500.00, matching ending_cash 4000.00 − beginning_cash 1500.00.

2027-12 and 2027 (full year): same end-of-year pattern as 2026 — December alone is quiet (net income 0.00), the full year's net income (1150.00) equals June's alone. Balance sheet after the second closing: assets (cash 4000.00 + inventory 750.00) 4750.00 = equity (owner_equity 2200.00 + retained_earnings 2550.00, 1400.00 + 1150.00 across both closings) 4750.00.
